# OrtoComune — Documento dei Requisiti

**Versione:** 0.1 (bozza) · **Data:** 2026-10-16
**Nota:** progetto interamente inventato, a scopo dimostrativo.

---

## 1. Visione e contesto

**OrtoComune** è una piattaforma web e mobile che aiuta i cittadini a gestire gli orti urbani condivisi del proprio quartiere. Permette di prenotare lotti, coordinare i turni di irrigazione e lavoro, scambiare sementi e attrezzi, e documentare i raccolti.

### 1.1 Problema
- I comitati di orti urbani gestiscono turni, quote e lotti con fogli di calcolo e chat di gruppo, con frequenti conflitti e dimenticanze.
- Gli ortolani esperti non hanno un canale semplice per condividere competenze con i principianti.
- Le amministrazioni comunali non hanno dati aggregati su utilizzo, raccolti e impatto ambientale.

### 1.2 Obiettivi
| ID | Obiettivo | Indicatore di successo |
|----|-----------|------------------------|
| OB-1 | Ridurre il tempo di coordinamento dei comitati | -50% di messaggi manuali sui turni entro 6 mesi dal lancio |
| OB-2 | Aumentare l'occupazione dei lotti | ≥ 85% dei lotti assegnati nei giardini aderenti |
| OB-3 | Favorire lo scambio di risorse | ≥ 300 scambi di sementi/attrezzi al mese a regime |
| OB-4 | Fornire dati d'impatto ai comuni | Report mensile automatico per ogni giardino |

### 1.3 Fuori ambito (v1)
- Vendita commerciale dei prodotti coltivati.
- Gestione di coltivazioni agricole professionali.
- Sensoristica IoT hardware (solo predisposizione API).

---

## 2. Attori e ruoli

| Ruolo | Descrizione |
|-------|-------------|
| **Ortolano** | Utente iscritto a uno o più giardini; gestisce il proprio lotto e partecipa ai turni. |
| **Ospite** | Utente non iscritto; può consultare giardini pubblici ed eventi. |
| **Referente di giardino** | Amministra un giardino: lotti, iscritti, quote, turni. |
| **Mentore** | Ortolano esperto che offre consulenza a principianti. |
| **Operatore comunale** | Consulta report aggregati e gestisce l'anagrafica dei giardini del proprio comune. |
| **Amministratore di piattaforma** | Gestione globale, moderazione, configurazione. |

---

## 3. Requisiti funzionali

Priorità secondo MoSCoW: **M** = Must, **S** = Should, **C** = Could.

### 3.1 Account e profilo
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-001 | Registrazione con email e password, con verifica dell'indirizzo email. | M |
| RF-002 | Accesso tramite provider esterni (Google, Apple). | S |
| RF-003 | Profilo con nome visualizzato, foto, quartiere, livello di esperienza e interessi colturali. | M |
| RF-004 | Recupero password tramite link temporaneo (validità 30 minuti). | M |
| RF-005 | Cancellazione account con esportazione preventiva dei dati personali. | M |
| RF-006 | Autenticazione a due fattori opzionale (TOTP). | C |

### 3.2 Giardini e lotti
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-010 | Ricerca di giardini per posizione, distanza e disponibilità di lotti, con vista mappa. | M |
| RF-011 | Scheda giardino: descrizione, foto, regolamento, servizi (acqua, compostiera, deposito attrezzi), orari. | M |
| RF-012 | Il referente definisce la planimetria del giardino come elenco di lotti con dimensione e stato (libero, assegnato, in manutenzione). | M |
| RF-013 | Richiesta di assegnazione lotto con lista d'attesa automatica ordinata per data di richiesta. | M |
| RF-014 | Il referente approva, rifiuta o riassegna le richieste; l'utente riceve una notifica. | M |
| RF-015 | Assegnazione con scadenza annuale e promemoria di rinnovo 30 e 7 giorni prima. | S |
| RF-016 | Possibilità di condividere un lotto tra più ortolani (lotto in co-gestione). | C |

### 3.3 Turni e attività comuni
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-020 | Calendario dei turni di irrigazione, pulizia e manutenzione delle aree comuni. | M |
| RF-021 | Iscrizione e disiscrizione ai turni; la disiscrizione entro 24 ore dall'inizio avvisa il referente. | M |
| RF-022 | Generazione automatica dei turni a rotazione in base a disponibilità dichiarate. | S |
| RF-023 | Registro delle presenze con conferma tramite QR code all'ingresso del giardino. | C |
| RF-024 | Sistema di punti "impegno" per chi svolge turni, visibile al referente. | C |
| RF-025 | Sospensione automatica dei turni in caso di allerta meteo (pioggia intensa, gelo). | S |

### 3.4 Diario colturale
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-030 | Registrazione di semine, trapianti, trattamenti e raccolti per ciascun lotto, con data, quantità e foto. | M |
| RF-031 | Catalogo di specie e varietà con calendario di semina consigliato per zona climatica. | M |
| RF-032 | Promemoria personalizzati per semina, annaffiatura e raccolta basati sul diario e sul meteo locale. | S |
| RF-033 | Riconoscimento di infestanti e malattie tramite foto con suggerimenti di rimedio biologico. | C |
| RF-034 | Statistiche personali: raccolto totale per specie, andamento stagionale. | S |

### 3.5 Scambi e comunità
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-040 | Bacheca scambi: annunci di sementi, piantine, attrezzi in prestito, eccedenze di raccolto. | M |
| RF-041 | Messaggistica diretta tra utenti dello stesso giardino o quartiere. | M |
| RF-042 | Prestito attrezzi con registro di consegna e restituzione e promemoria di scadenza. | S |
| RF-043 | Forum per giardino con thread, risposte e segnalazione dei contenuti. | S |
| RF-044 | Programma Mentore: richiesta e assegnazione di un mentore per una stagione. | C |
| RF-045 | Eventi del giardino (workshop, giornate di raccolta) con iscrizione e capienza massima. | S |

### 3.6 Quote e pagamenti
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-050 | Il referente configura la quota annuale e le eventuali quote straordinarie. | M |
| RF-051 | Pagamento della quota online con carta o wallet digitale. | S |
| RF-052 | Ricevuta digitale scaricabile in PDF. | S |
| RF-053 | Cruscotto del referente con stato dei pagamenti e solleciti automatici. | S |

### 3.7 Notifiche
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-060 | Notifiche push (mobile), email e in-app configurabili per categoria. | M |
| RF-061 | Riepilogo settimanale via email delle attività del giardino. | C |
| RF-062 | Orari di silenzio configurabili dall'utente. | S |

### 3.8 Funzioni comunali e report
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-070 | Dashboard comunale con occupazione dei lotti, utenti attivi e raccolto stimato per giardino. | S |
| RF-071 | Stima del risparmio di CO₂ e dei rifiuti organici compostati. | C |
| RF-072 | Esportazione dei report in CSV e PDF. | S |

### 3.9 Amministrazione di piattaforma
| ID | Requisito | Pri. |
|----|-----------|------|
| RF-080 | Moderazione dei contenuti segnalati con storico delle azioni. | M |
| RF-081 | Gestione dei comuni e dei giardini aderenti, inclusa l'attivazione di nuovi giardini. | M |
| RF-082 | Gestione del catalogo specie/varietà e dei testi legali. | S |

---

## 4. Requisiti specifici per piattaforma

### 4.1 Web
- RW-01: Applicazione responsive utilizzabile da 360 px di larghezza in su. (M)
- RW-02: Area di amministrazione per referenti e operatori comunali ottimizzata per desktop, con tabelle filtrabili e ordinabili. (M)
- RW-03: Supporto agli ultimi due rilasci principali di Chrome, Firefox, Safari ed Edge. (M)
- RW-04: Pagine pubbliche dei giardini indicizzabili dai motori di ricerca (rendering lato server). (S)

### 4.2 Mobile (iOS e Android)
- RM-01: App nativa o cross-platform per iOS 16+ e Android 10+. (M)
- RM-02: Funzionamento offline per consultazione del diario e inserimento di note; sincronizzazione alla riconnessione con risoluzione dei conflitti "ultima modifica prevale" segnalata all'utente. (M)
- RM-03: Acquisizione foto da fotocamera con compressione prima del caricamento. (M)
- RM-04: Scansione QR per presenze e restituzione attrezzi. (C)
- RM-05: Widget per la schermata home con il prossimo turno e il meteo del giardino. (C)
- RM-06: Accesso biometrico dopo il primo login. (S)

---

## 5. Requisiti non funzionali

### 5.1 Prestazioni
- RNF-01: Tempo di risposta API al 95° percentile inferiore a 400 ms con 2.000 utenti concorrenti.
- RNF-02: Caricamento della schermata iniziale mobile entro 2 secondi su rete 4G.
- RNF-03: Caricamento della pagina pubblica di un giardino con LCP inferiore a 2,5 secondi.

### 5.2 Disponibilità e affidabilità
- RNF-10: Disponibilità mensile ≥ 99,5% escluse manutenzioni programmate.
- RNF-11: Backup giornalieri con conservazione per 30 giorni; RPO ≤ 24 ore, RTO ≤ 4 ore.
- RNF-12: Degradazione controllata: in caso di indisponibilità del servizio meteo, le funzioni principali restano operative.

### 5.3 Sicurezza e privacy
- RNF-20: Conformità al GDPR: consenso esplicito, registro dei trattamenti, diritto all'oblio e alla portabilità.
- RNF-21: Password memorizzate con algoritmo di hashing adattivo; traffico esclusivamente su TLS 1.2+.
- RNF-22: Controllo degli accessi basato sui ruoli applicato lato server su ogni endpoint.
- RNF-23: La posizione esatta dei lotti e le generalità degli utenti non sono visibili agli ospiti; la posizione dell'utente non è mai condivisa senza consenso.
- RNF-24: Rate limiting su autenticazione e messaggistica; log di audit per azioni amministrative.
- RNF-25: Penetration test esterno prima del lancio e a cadenza annuale.

### 5.4 Usabilità e accessibilità
- RNF-30: Conformità WCAG 2.2 livello AA.
- RNF-31: Interfaccia in italiano e inglese; architettura predisposta per ulteriori lingue.
- RNF-32: Un nuovo utente completa iscrizione e richiesta di un lotto in meno di 5 minuti (test di usabilità con almeno 8 partecipanti).
- RNF-33: Supporto a dimensione del testo di sistema ingrandita e modalità scura.

### 5.5 Manutenibilità e osservabilità
- RNF-40: Copertura dei test automatici ≥ 70% sul codice di business.
- RNF-41: Pipeline CI/CD con rilascio automatico in ambiente di staging e approvazione manuale per la produzione.
- RNF-42: Logging strutturato, metriche e allarmi su errori e latenza.

### 5.6 Scalabilità
- RNF-50: Architettura in grado di crescere fino a 500 giardini e 100.000 utenti registrati senza riprogettazione.

---

## 6. Modello dati (alto livello)

Entità principali e relazioni:

- **Utente** 1—N **Iscrizione** N—1 **Giardino**
- **Giardino** 1—N **Lotto**; **Lotto** 1—N **Assegnazione** (storica) N—1 **Utente**
- **Giardino** 1—N **Turno** 1—N **Partecipazione** N—1 **Utente**
- **Lotto** 1—N **VoceDiario** N—1 **Varietà**
- **Utente** 1—N **Annuncio**; **Annuncio** 1—N **Conversazione**
- **Giardino** 1—N **Quota** 1—N **Pagamento**
- **Giardino** 1—N **Evento** 1—N **IscrizioneEvento**

---

## 7. Integrazioni esterne

| Integrazione | Scopo | Pri. |
|--------------|-------|------|
| Servizio meteo | Previsioni, allerte e promemoria di irrigazione | M |
| Provider di mappe | Ricerca e visualizzazione dei giardini | M |
| Gateway di pagamento | Quote online | S |
| Servizio di notifiche push (APNs/FCM) | Notifiche mobile | M |
| Servizio email transazionale | Verifiche, ricevute, riepiloghi | M |
| Servizio di riconoscimento immagini | Diagnosi piante da foto | C |
| API aperte (sola lettura) | Dati aggregati per comuni e università | C |

---

## 8. Vincoli e assunzioni

**Vincoli**
- V-1: Budget di sviluppo della prima release limitato a un team di 6 persone per 7 mesi.
- V-2: I dati devono risiedere in data center nell'Unione Europea.
- V-3: Lancio pilota previsto in 4 giardini di una sola città prima dell'espansione.

**Assunzioni**
- A-1: Almeno un referente per giardino è disposto a usare lo strumento in sostituzione dei canali attuali.
- A-2: La maggior parte degli ortolani possiede uno smartphone con fotocamera.
- A-3: I comuni aderenti forniscono l'anagrafica dei giardini in formato elettronico.

---

## 9. Rischi

| ID | Rischio | Probabilità | Impatto | Mitigazione |
|----|---------|-------------|---------|-------------|
| R-1 | Scarsa adozione da parte di utenti poco digitalizzati | Alta | Alto | Assistenza in presenza nel pilota, modalità semplificata, guide stampabili |
| R-2 | Connettività scarsa nei giardini | Media | Medio | Funzionamento offline (RM-02) |
| R-3 | Dispute sull'assegnazione dei lotti | Media | Medio | Regole trasparenti, lista d'attesa tracciata, audit |
| R-4 | Costi elevati del riconoscimento immagini | Media | Basso | Funzione "Could", limite di richieste per utente |
| R-5 | Violazione di dati personali | Bassa | Alto | RNF-20…25, piano di risposta agli incidenti |

---

## 10. Criteri di accettazione per le funzioni chiave

**Richiesta di un lotto (RF-013/014)**
- Dato un utente iscritto a un giardino senza lotti liberi, quando invia la richiesta, allora viene inserito in lista d'attesa con posizione visibile.
- Dato un lotto che si libera, quando il referente lo assegna al primo in lista, allora l'utente riceve una notifica entro 1 minuto e la lista si aggiorna.

**Disiscrizione da un turno (RF-021)**
- Dato un turno che inizia tra meno di 24 ore, quando l'utente si disiscrive, allora il referente riceve una notifica e il turno risulta "scoperto".

**Sincronizzazione offline (RM-02)**
- Dato un utente senza connessione, quando crea due voci di diario, allora sono salvate localmente e inviate automaticamente al ripristino della rete, senza duplicati.

**Cancellazione account (RF-005)**
- Dato un utente che richiede la cancellazione, quando conferma, allora i dati personali sono rimossi entro 30 giorni e gli annunci pubblici anonimizzati.

---

## 11. Piano di rilascio proposto

| Fase | Contenuto | Durata |
|------|-----------|--------|
| **MVP (pilota)** | Account, giardini e lotti, turni, diario base, notifiche, bacheca scambi | 4 mesi |
| **Release 1.0** | Quote e pagamenti, eventi, forum, offline completo, dashboard comunale | 3 mesi |
| **Release 1.x** | Mentori, riconoscimento immagini, widget, API aperte, report d'impatto | continuativo |

---

## 12. Glossario

- **Lotto:** porzione di terreno assegnata a un ortolano o a un gruppo.
- **Referente:** volontario o dipendente responsabile della gestione di un giardino.
- **Turno:** attività comune a carico dei soci in una fascia oraria definita.
- **Mentore:** ortolano che affianca un principiante per una stagione.

data.envs: Dev: sviluppo, può essere instabile; QA manuale durante lo sprint. Test: QA del fornitore, automation e regressione. Staging: collaudo del Comune prima del rilascio e prove del pilota. Produzione: utenti finali. Il report QA va al Product Owner prima di ogni promozione in Staging.

data.constraints: V-1: team di 6 persone per 7 mesi (2 back-end/cloud, 1 web, 1 mobile cross-platform, 1 UX/UI, 1 QA con automation) per MVP e Release 1.0; la Release 1.x è finanziata a parte. V-2: tutti i dati personali e il provider cloud in data center UE, anche per email, notifiche, meteo e riconoscimento immagini. V-3: pilota in 4 giardini di una sola città (Comune di Montelupo), avvio indicativo 2027-03-15; l'MVP non può slittare oltre aprile 2027. Un solo marchio (OrtoComune), nessun white label. Nessun firmware né dispositivo fisico; sensoristica IoT fuori ambito. Web responsive da 360 px; iOS 16+ e Android 10+ con app Flutter unica. Età minima di registrazione 16 anni. Titolare del trattamento: il Comune. Testi legali forniti dal Comune in italiano e inglese entro dicembre 2026. Priorità e release decise da Elena Marchetti; UX approvata da Giorgio Bellini; riferimento tecnico Davide Sala. Sprint di due settimane, planning il lunedì mattina. Rilascio in Staging ogni due settimane il giovedì pomeriggio, mai il venerdì, con via libera di Elena Marchetti dopo il report QA. Design in Figma, documentazione tecnica in Confluence, documento dei requisiti come fonte contrattuale. Progetto Jira esistente COM, nessun campo custom obbligatorio. Se serve tagliare, si toglie prima ciò che è Could (RF-023, RF-024, RF-016).

data.ui: Elenco annunci, creazione annuncio con foto, filtri.

data.title: Notifiche configurabili per categoria

data.questions: Priorità Should: va confermato se è nell'MVP. Non è detto se le notifiche urgenti siano escluse dal silenzio.

data.questions: Release non indicata. Non è chiaro se gli attrezzi siano personali o del giardino. Non è chiaro se la conferma richieda entrambe le parti.

data.ui: Coda di moderazione e storico nell'area di amministrazione.

data.questions: Release non indicata. Non è definito il livello di compressione.

data.q: Lingua e tono verso il cliente.
data.answer: Verso il cliente italiano, registro formale e frasi brevi, senza gergo tecnico. I documenti contrattuali anche in inglese se richiesti.

data.q: Progetto nel tracker esistente o da creare? Campi custom obbligatori?
data.answer: Progetto Jira esistente (COM). Nessun campo custom obbligatorio oltre a quelli standard; le label seguono il playbook.

data.q: Il test di usabilità di RNF-32 (almeno 8 partecipanti) e il penetration test esterno di RNF-25 richiedono reclutamento e un fornitore esterno. Chi li organizza, con quale budget e in quale finestra prima del lancio pilota?
data.answer: Il fornitore organizza il test di usabilità con 8 partecipanti reclutati dal Comune a gennaio 2027. Il penetration test esterno lo commissiona il Comune a un fornitore certificato, con budget separato, entro febbraio 2027, prima del pilota.

data.q: Per RNF-20 (GDPR) chi è il titolare del trattamento e chi redige i testi legali, l'informativa privacy e il registro dei trattamenti? I testi legali (RF-082) sono forniti dal cliente in italiano e inglese? Quale è l'età minima per la registrazione?
data.answer: Titolare del trattamento è il Comune. I testi legali (informativa privacy, registro dei trattamenti, termini d'uso) li redige l'ufficio legale del Comune in italiano e inglese entro dicembre 2026. Età minima per la registrazione: 16 anni.

data.q: Quali piattaforme: Web, iOS, Android, cloud, firmware, dispositivi?
data.answer: Web App responsive (da 360 px) e app mobile per iOS 16+ e Android 10+, con back-end cloud. Nessun firmware né dispositivo fisico: le sensoristiche IoT restano fuori ambito.

data.q: Esistono versioni white label o per altri marchi, e con quali differenze?
data.answer: No: nessuna versione white label nell'MVP né nella Release 1.0. Un solo marchio, OrtoComune. L'eventuale personalizzazione per altri comuni si valuta dopo la Release 1.x.

data.q: Quali requisiti dipendono da hardware, firmware o librerie non ancora disponibili?
data.answer: Nessun requisito dipende da hardware o firmware. Le dipendenze esterne sono servizi di terzi: provider di mappe, servizio meteo (RF-025, RNF-12), riconoscimento immagini (RF-033), gateway di pagamento (RF-051), Google Sign-In e Sign in with Apple (RF-002), APNs e FCM.

data.q: Chi compone il team interno, con quali ruoli e quali componenti?
data.answer: 6 persone per 7 mesi (V-1): 2 sviluppatori back-end/cloud, 1 web, 1 mobile (cross-platform), 1 UX/UI e 1 QA con automation. Il Product Owner è un ruolo a parte.

data.q: Chi fa QA manuale e automatico, su quale ambiente.
data.answer: QA manuale su Dev durante lo sprint, QA automation e regressione su Test. Il report QA va al Product Owner prima di ogni promozione in Staging.

data.q: Sono previste regole per l'MVP sulla sede del pilota (città, comune partner, 4 giardini già individuati)? Serve una configurazione multi-comune fin dall'MVP o basta un solo comune? Questo incide su RF-081 e sulla zona climatica del catalogo (RF-031).
data.answer: Nell'MVP un solo comune partner (Comune di Montelupo) con i 4 giardini già individuati. La configurazione multi-comune arriva in Release 1.0. La zona climatica del catalogo (RF-031) è fissata per quel comune.

data.q: Le sensoristiche IoT sono fuori ambito con sola predisposizione API. Cosa si intende per predisposizione API e va creato un ticket? Sono previsti dispositivi fisici per i QR code all'ingresso (RF-023, RM-04), chi li produce e li installa e serve lavoro firmware?

## Context
Requirement RF-001: users must be able to register with email and password and verify their email address. The back-end must provide the data model, APIs and rules for both Web App and Mobile App. Personal data and the email service must be hosted in EU data centers (constraint V-2).

## User story
As a prospective gardener, I want to register with my email and password and verify my email address, so that I can have a trusted account on OrtoComune.

## Scope / Action
* Create the user account data model (email, password hash, verification status, creation date, consent records).
* Implement the registration API with email format and password rule validation, and rejection of already registered emails.
* Hash passwords with a state-of-the-art algorithm; never store or log them in clear text.
* Generate a time-limited, single-use verification token and send the verification email through the transactional email service.
* Implement the verification API and a resend-verification API with rate limiting.
* Enforce the minimum registration age of 16 years as agreed.
* Record acceptance of terms and privacy notice with version and timestamp.
* Use an email provider and storage located in the EU.
* Keep the API contract versioned and usable by both clients.

## Dependencies
* Choice of the transactional email service (external dependency).
* Legal texts from the Municipality (Italian and English) for email content and consent versions.

## Points to clarify
* Password policy: minimum length and complexity. Options: length only (e.g. 10+ characters) or length plus character classes.
* Verification link validity: 24 hours or 72 hours.
* Can an unverified user log in? Options: no access until verified, or limited access with a reminder.
* How is the age of 16 checked? Options: self-declaration checkbox, or date of birth field.
* Which transactional email provider in the EU is chosen.

## Acceptance criteria
* A new user can register with a valid email and password and receives a verification email.
* Registration with an already used email is rejected with a clear error without exposing account details.
* Passwords are stored only as hashes.
* The verification link confirms the email once; reuse or an expired link returns a specific error.
* A resend request issues a new token and invalidates the previous one; excessive requests are rate limited.
* A user who does not meet the minimum age cannot complete registration.
* Acceptance of terms is stored with version and timestamp.
* All personal data and emails are processed in EU data centers.
* Automated tests cover registration, verification, expiry and resend.

## References
* Requirement RF-001.
* Constraint V-2 (EU data hosting).

## Context
Requirement RF-002: users can sign in with Google or Apple. The back-end must validate provider identity tokens, create or match user accounts and issue sessions for Web App and Mobile App. It depends on the account model from RF-001. Personal data must stay in EU data centers (constraint V-2).

## User story
As a gardener, I want to sign in with my Google or Apple account, so that I can access OrtoComune without creating a separate password.

## Scope / Action
* Integrate Google Sign-In and Sign in with Apple token validation on the server side.
* Create a new account on first social sign-in, reusing the user model from RF-001 and marking the email as verified when the provider asserts it.
* Link social identities to existing accounts according to the agreed rule.
* Handle Apple private relay emails and the case of missing email.
* Enforce the minimum age of 16 and the acceptance of terms for accounts created via social sign-in.
* Store only the data needed from providers (provider ID, email, name).
* Do not break the RF-001 registration and login APIs.

## Dependencies
* RF-001 account model and registration API must be done first.
* Configuration of Google and Apple developer accounts and credentials (external dependency).

## Points to clarify
* Account linking: when a social email matches an existing email/password account, link automatically (only if the email is verified) or ask the user to sign in first.
* Handling of Apple private relay addresses for notifications and communication.
* Which data is collected after first social sign-in (terms, age confirmation).
* Who owns the Google and Apple developer accounts.

## Acceptance criteria
* A user can sign in with a valid Google identity token and obtains a session.
* A user can sign in with a valid Apple identity token and obtains a session.
* Invalid or expired provider tokens are rejected.
* A first-time social user gets an account; a returning user is matched to the same account.
* The linking rule with an existing email account is applied as decided and creates no duplicates.
* Users who do not meet the age requirement or have not accepted terms cannot complete account creation.
* Personal data is stored in EU data centers.
* Automated tests cover new user, returning user, linking and invalid token.

## References
* Requirement RF-002.
* Requirement RF-001 (internal dependency).
* Constraint V-2.

## Context
Requirement RF-003: users can manage a profile with display name, photo, neighbourhood, experience level and gardening interests. The back-end must store the profile data and photos and expose APIs for Web App and Mobile App. Personal data and photos must be stored in EU data centers (constraint V-2). It builds on the user account from RF-001.

## User story
As a gardener, I want to manage my profile with name, photo, neighbourhood, experience level and interests, so that other members and referents can know me and the app can adapt to me.

## Scope / Action
* Create the profile data model linked to the user account: display name, photo reference, neighbourhood, experience level, gardening interests.
* Implement APIs to read and update the profile of the authenticated user.
* Implement photo upload, replacement and removal with file type and size validation, and image resizing.
* Store photos in EU-hosted object storage and serve them through controlled URLs.
* Validate fields (length, allowed values) and return clear errors.
* Allow only the owner to edit their profile.
* Keep the API compatible with the RF-001 account APIs.

## Dependencies
* RF-001 user account model must be done first.

## Points to clarify
* Neighbourhood: free text or a list defined per garden or city (Montelupo).
* Experience level values: e.g. beginner, intermediate, expert.
* Gardening interests: fixed list or free tags, and who maintains the list.
* Photo limits: maximum size and allowed formats.
* Profile visibility: which fields are visible to other members, referents and guests.
* Moderation of profile photos.

## Acceptance criteria
* An authenticated user can read and update display name, neighbourhood, experience level and interests.
* A user can upload, replace and remove a profile photo within the agreed limits.
* Invalid files and invalid field values are rejected with clear errors.
* A user cannot read private fields or edit the profile of another user.
* Photos and profile data are stored in EU data centers.
* Automated tests cover update, photo upload and permission checks.

## References
* Requirement RF-003.
* Requirement RF-001 (internal dependency).
* Constraint V-2.

data.desc:
## Context
RF-004 requires that users can recover their password through a temporary link valid for 30 minutes. The back-end must generate and validate reset tokens and send the email through the transactional email service. It depends on the registration and login of RF-001.

## User story
As a registered user who forgot the password, I want to receive a temporary reset link by email, so that I can set a new password and access my account again.

## Scope / Action
* API to request a reset by email address, with a neutral response whether or not the account exists.
* Generate a random single-use token, store only its hash, expiry 30 minutes.
* Send the reset email through the transactional email service (provider and data in an EU data center, constraint V-2).
* API to validate the token and set the new password, applying the same password rules as registration.
* Invalidate the token after use or expiry, and invalidate previous tokens when a new one is requested.
* Rate limiting on reset requests.
* Must not break: existing login and registration (RF-001).

## Dependencies
* RF-001 (registration and login) must be available.
* Transactional email service selected and configured in the EU.

## Points to clarify
* Email texts and languages (Italian only or Italian and English).
* Whether a successful reset closes all active sessions (proposed: yes).
* Rate limit values.
* Behaviour for accounts with two-factor authentication active (RF-006): reset password only, 2FA still required at login (proposed).

## Acceptance criteria
* A reset request for an existing email sends one email with a link valid for 30 minutes.
* A reset request for an unknown email returns the same response and sends no email.
* A link used after 30 minutes is rejected with an expiry error.
* A link can be used only once.
* After a successful reset the user can log in with the new password and not with the old one.
* A password not meeting the rules is rejected with a clear error.
* No personal data is processed outside the EU.

## References
* Requirement RF-004
* Requirement RF-001

## Context
Requirement RF-021 states that when a gardener withdraws less than 24 hours before the start of a shift, the referent is alerted. This needs the notification services (push and email) from RF-060. This is a distinct back-end job from the enrollment rules.

## User story
As a referent, I want to be alerted when a gardener withdraws from a shift at the last minute, so that I can find a replacement in time.

## Scope / Action
* Trigger an alert to the referent of the garden when a late withdrawal marks a shift as uncovered.
* Send the alert by push notification and by email.
* Content of the alert: garden, shift type, common area, date and time, name of the gardener who withdrew.
* Avoid duplicate alerts for the same withdrawal.
* Handle delivery failure with retry and logging.
* Use only push and email providers hosted in EU data centers.
* Compatibility: do not block the withdrawal if the alert fails.

## Dependencies
* Enrollment, withdrawal and uncovered state (RF-021) must be done first.
* Push notification service and email service (RF-060) must be available.

## Points to clarify
* Who receives the alert if a garden has more than one referent: all of them or only the primary one?
* Should the alert include the name of the gardener who withdrew (privacy)? Proposed: yes.
* Do referents have preferences to disable push or email?
* Text of the alert in Italian and English: who approves it?

## Acceptance criteria
* A late withdrawal sends one alert to the referent by push and by email.
* A withdrawal outside the 24-hour window sends no alert.
* A failure of the push or email service does not cancel the withdrawal and is retried and logged.
* No duplicate alert is sent for the same withdrawal.
* Providers and data are in EU data centers.
* Automated tests cover the trigger and the failure case.

## References
* Requirement RF-021.
* Related requirement: RF-060.

## Context
Requirement RF-013 allows a member of a garden to request a plot. When no plot is free, the request goes into a waiting list ordered by request date. The position must be visible to the user. The back-end must provide data and rules before the front-ends can be built.

## User story
As a garden member, I want to request a plot and see my position in the waiting list, so that I know when I can expect an assignment.

## Scope / Action
* Data model for plot requests: user, garden, request date, status, waiting list position.
* API to create a plot request, only for users enrolled in the garden.
* If a free plot exists, the request is created as pending for the referent decision (see RF-014). If none is free, it is added to the waiting list.
* Waiting list ordered by request date (oldest first). Position computed by the back-end and returned by the API.
* API to read the status and position of own requests.
* Rule against duplicate active requests by the same user in the same garden.
* Personal data stored only in EU data centers (constraint V-2).
* Must stay compatible with the plot data defined in RF-012.

## Dependencies
* Plot data model and plot availability from requirement RF-012.
* Request management by the referent from requirement RF-014 (shared status model).

## Points to clarify
* Does a request create a pending item even when a plot is free, or is the plot assigned directly? Option A: always pending for referent approval. Option B: automatic assignment.
* Can a user request more than one plot in the same garden? Option A: one active request only. Option B: multiple.
* Can the user withdraw a request? Option A: yes, position recalculated. Option B: no.
* Tie-break for requests with the same timestamp.

## Acceptance criteria
* An enrolled user can create a plot request through the API.
* A user not enrolled in the garden receives an authorization error.
* When no plot is free, the request is placed in the waiting list ordered by request date.
* The API returns the correct position of the user in the waiting list.
* Positions are recalculated when a request is removed or assigned.
* A duplicate active request is rejected with a clear error.
* Automated API tests cover the cases above.

## References
* Requirement RF-013 (source document).
* Related requirements: RF-012, RF-014.

## Context
Requirement RF-014 lets the referent approve, reject or reassign plot requests. The user must be notified. In case of assignment, the notification must arrive within 1 minute.

## User story
As a referent, I want to approve, reject or reassign plot requests, so that plots are assigned to the right members and they are informed quickly.

## Scope / Action
* API to list the plot requests of the garden managed by the referent.
* API to approve, reject and reassign a request, with authorization limited to the referent of that garden.
* On approval, the plot is assigned to the user and the waiting list is updated.
* On reassignment, the request is moved to another free plot and the previous plot is released.
* Trigger of push and email notifications to the user for each decision, using the notification service (RF-060).
* Assignment notification delivered within 1 minute from the decision.
* Audit trail of decisions: who, when, previous and new status.
* EU data centers only for notification and email providers (constraint V-2).
* Must not break the request data and statuses from RF-013.

## Dependencies
* Plot request API and waiting list (RF-013).
* Notification service for push and email (RF-060).

## Points to clarify
* Is a rejection reason mandatory? Option A: optional. Option B: mandatory.
* Which notifications must be sent for rejection and reassignment? Option A: same channels as assignment. Option B: push only.
* The 1 minute target applies to assignment only. Is a target needed for the other decisions?
* Can a request be reassigned to a plot of another garden? Option A: no. Option B: yes.

## Acceptance criteria
* Only the referent of the garden can approve, reject or reassign its requests.
* Approval assigns the plot and updates the waiting list positions.
* Rejection updates the request status and notifies the user.
* Reassignment releases the previous plot and assigns the new one.
* The user receives the assignment notification within 1 minute in at least 95% of tests under normal load.
* Concurrent decisions on the same request are handled without double assignment.
* Automated API tests cover the cases above.

## References
* Requirement RF-014 (source document).
* Related requirements: RF-013, RF-060.

## Context
Requirement RF-015: a plot assignment expires one year after the assignment. The user must receive renewal reminders 30 and 7 days before expiry. The back-end must manage expiry dates, the renewal action and the reminder scheduling.

## User story
As a garden member with an assigned plot, I want to be reminded before my assignment expires and to renew it, so that I do not lose my plot by mistake.

## Scope / Action
* Expiry date stored on every plot assignment: assignment date plus one year.
* API to read the expiry date and the renewal state of own assignments.
* API for the renewal action, updating the expiry date.
* Scheduled job that sends reminders 30 and 7 days before expiry through the notification service (RF-060), push and email.
* Each reminder sent only once per assignment and per renewal cycle.
* Reminders cancelled or not sent if the assignment is already renewed or released.
* Handling of expired assignments: status update and plot release according to the decision below.
* EU data centers only for notification and email providers (constraint V-2).
* Must not break assignment data from RF-014.

## Dependencies
* Plot assignment flow (RF-014).
* Notification service for push and email (RF-060).
* RF-050, as indicated in the requirement dependencies (content to be confirmed).

## Points to clarify
* Is the renewal automatic on request or does it need the referent approval? Option A: automatic. Option B: approval by the referent.
* What happens at expiry without renewal? Option A: the plot is released and the waiting list is used. Option B: the plot stays blocked until the referent decides.
* Time zone and time of day for the reminders. Option: Europe/Rome, morning.
* Does the new expiry start from the old expiry date or from the renewal date?
* Which role does RF-050 play in this requirement?

## Acceptance criteria
* Every new assignment has an expiry date exactly one year after the assignment date.
* The user receives a reminder 30 days before expiry and another 7 days before expiry.
* No duplicate reminders are sent for the same assignment and cycle.
* No reminder is sent after a renewal or release of the assignment.
* The renewal action updates the expiry date and the new reminders are scheduled.
* Expired assignments follow the rule decided by the PO.
* Automated tests cover the scheduling and the renewal.

## References
* Requirement RF-015 (source document).
* Related requirements: RF-014, RF-060, RF-050.

## Context
Requirement RF-025: the system must automatically suspend shifts when a weather alert (heavy rain, frost) is issued and inform the enrolled members. The back-end must read alerts from an external weather service, change the shift state and trigger notifications.

## User story
As a garden member enrolled in a shift, I want the shift to be suspended automatically when a weather alert is issued and to be informed, so that I do not go to the garden in unsafe conditions.

## Scope / Action
* Integrate the external weather service to retrieve alerts for the location of each garden (heavy rain, frost).
* Add the "suspended" state to the shift data model, with reason, alert type and timestamp.
* Scheduled job that evaluates upcoming shifts against active alerts and suspends the affected ones.
* Handle alert withdrawal: rule for resuming a suspended shift (to be confirmed).
* Trigger a notification to all enrolled members through the notification capability (RF-060).
* Expose the suspended state and reason through the shift API for Web and Mobile clients.
* Keep existing shift API backward compatible: new state must not break current clients.
* All personal data and the weather integration must stay in EU data centres (constraint V-2); no personal data sent to the weather provider.
* Log every automatic suspension for audit.

## Dependencies
* RF-020 (shifts) must be available.
* RF-060 (notifications) must be available.
* RNF-12 to be checked.
* Selection and contract of the weather service.

## Points to clarify
* Weather provider: which one, and is it hosted or processed in the EU? (PO / client)
* Alert thresholds: use the official alert levels or custom thresholds for rain and frost? (PO)
* Suspension window: how many hours before the shift is it evaluated? (PO)
* After suspension: is the shift cancelled, rescheduled or resumed automatically if the alert ends? (PO / client)
* Can a referent override a suspension manually? (PO)
* Notification channels: push only, or push and email? (PO)

## Acceptance criteria
* When an active alert of a configured type covers a garden, the affected shifts in the evaluation window are set to "suspended" automatically.
* Every enrolled member of a suspended shift receives a notification with the reason.
* The shift API returns the suspended state and the reason.
* Shifts not affected by the alert are unchanged.
* A suspension is not applied twice and does not send duplicate notifications.
* If the weather service is unavailable, no shift is changed and the error is logged.
* No personal data is stored or processed outside the EU.

## References
* Requirement RF-025.
* Related requirements: RF-020, RF-060, RNF-12.
* Design: Spike for the suspended shift state (same requirement).

## Context
RF-060 requires push notifications on mobile and email notifications, sent according to user preferences. This work covers the delivery channels and their providers. Other features, such as direct messaging (RF-041), use it to alert users.

As a gardener, I want to receive push and email notifications for the categories I enabled, so that I do not miss messages and activities.

## Scope / Action
* Integrate APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android) for push, with device token registration and removal.
* Integrate a transactional email service with EU data processing (constraint V-2).
* Email templates in Italian and English, single brand OrtoComune.
* Delivery pipeline: receive an event, check user preferences, send on enabled channels, record the outcome.
* Retry and failure handling, with invalid tokens removed.
* Compatibility: the event interface must be usable by RF-041 and other features without change.

## Dependencies
* Preferences API from the notification centre and preferences ticket.
* Accounts with APNs and FCM credentials, and a transactional email provider (external).

## Points to clarify
* Choice of the email provider, which must process data in the EU. Options to be proposed by the technical reference.
* Email sender address and domain, to be provided by the Comune.
* Language of notifications: user language, or Italian by default.
* Sending limits: grouping of frequent notifications (for example many messages in a short time).
* Email notifications for users who never installed the app.

## Acceptance criteria
* A mobile user with push enabled for a category receives a push on iOS and on Android.
* A user with email enabled for a category receives an email.
* No notification is sent on a channel disabled in the preferences.
* Invalid device tokens are removed after a failed delivery.
* Providers and stored data comply with the EU data center constraint.

* Requirement RF-060.
* Related requirements RF-041.
* External dependencies: APNs/FCM, transactional email service.

data.desc:
## Context
Requirement RF-061 asks for a weekly email summary of garden activities for the user. The email template is not designed yet. The feature relies on the transactional email service and on RF-060. All personal data and the email provider must stay in EU data centers (constraint V-2).

## User story
As a gardener, I want to receive a weekly email summarising the activities of my garden, so that I stay informed without opening the app.

## Scope / Action
* Build a weekly scheduled job that collects, for each recipient, the activities of the gardens they belong to.
* Render the summary into an email template and send it through the transactional email service.
* Send only to users who have an email address and who have not opted out, as defined by the notification preferences (RF-060).
* Avoid duplicate sends if the job runs twice. Log failures and retry them.
* Use an EU-hosted email provider (V-2). Do not include more personal data than needed.
* Do not break the existing notification mechanisms from RF-060.

## Dependencies
* RF-060 (notification preferences and delivery) must be available.
* Transactional email service selected and configured in an EU region.
* Approved email template content and layout.

## Points to clarify
* Day and time of the weekly send. Options: Monday morning, or Sunday evening.
* Content of the summary: shifts, diary entries, exchanges, or other. To be confirmed by the PO.
* Language of the email: Italian only, or Italian and English by user preference.
* Whether the summary respects quiet hours (RF-062). Options: always send, or defer to the next allowed time.
* Whether a user with no activity in the week still receives an email.
* Whether the user can unsubscribe from this email only, or only from all emails.

## Acceptance criteria
* Each eligible user receives at most one summary email per week.
* The summary lists the garden activities of the previous week.
* Users who opted out do not receive the email.
* A failed send is logged and retried, and does not block other recipients.
* Email service and data processing are in EU data centers.
* The email uses the approved template.

## References
* Requirement RF-061
* Depends on requirement RF-060
* Email template design: not yet available

## Context
Requirement RF-062 lets a user configure hours in which they receive no notifications. The feature involves Web App, Mobile App and Back-end/Cloud. The design is not ready, so only the back-end part is described here. It depends on RF-060.

## User story
As a gardener, I want to set quiet hours, so that I do not receive notifications at times when I do not want to be disturbed.

## Scope / Action
* Store per user the quiet hours setting: start time, end time, enabled flag.
* Expose API to read and update the setting, with validation of values.
* Apply the setting in the notification delivery flow from RF-060: notifications generated in the quiet window are not delivered during it.
* Interpret times in the user's time zone, or in a single default time zone.
* Do not break existing notification delivery and preferences from RF-060.
* Keep personal data in EU data centers (V-2).

## Dependencies
* RF-060 (notification delivery and preferences).
* The UX spike for the setting, before FE tickets are created.

## Points to clarify
* Behaviour for notifications generated during quiet hours. Options: discard, or hold and deliver when the quiet window ends.
* Whether the setting applies to all channels (push, email) or only to push.
* Whether urgent or administrative notifications can bypass quiet hours.
* Time zone handling. Options: single zone (Europe/Rome) or per-user zone.
* Whether a window crossing midnight is allowed (for example 22:00 to 07:00).
* Default value for new users: disabled, or a default window.

## Acceptance criteria
* A user can save and read back their quiet hours through the API.
* Invalid values are rejected with a clear error.
* No notification is delivered to the user inside their quiet window, according to the decided behaviour.
* A window crossing midnight is handled correctly, if allowed by the decision.
* Notifications outside the quiet window are delivered as before.
* Automated tests cover the window boundaries.

## References
* Requirement RF-062
* Depends on requirement RF-060
* Design frames: not yet available

## Context
Requirement RNF-42 asks that the system provides structured logging, metrics and alerts on errors and latency. This is a non-functional requirement for the back-end/cloud component, needed from the pilot (MVP) so that the team can detect and diagnose problems in the 4 pilot gardens. All data, including logs and metrics, must stay in EU data centers (constraint V-2).

## User story
As a platform administrator, I want structured logs, metrics and alerts on errors and latency, so that I can detect and diagnose incidents quickly during the pilot.

## Scope / Action
* Introduce structured logging (JSON format) in all back-end services, with a common set of fields (timestamp, level, service, request ID, endpoint, status, duration).
* Make sure logs never contain personal data in clear text (emails, names, tokens); mask or omit them.
* Collect request metrics: request count, error rate, latency (p50, p95, p99) per endpoint.
* Configure alerts on error rate and latency above agreed thresholds, with notification to the technical reference.
* Create a basic dashboard for logs and metrics, available in Staging and Production.
* Host the logging, metrics and alerting tools in an EU data center; set a log retention period.
* Must not break existing APIs or add noticeable latency to requests.

## Dependencies
* Cloud environments (Staging and Production) available in an EU region.
* Choice of the monitoring tool and the alert channel.

## Points to clarify
* Monitoring tool: managed service of the cloud provider (EU region) or self-hosted open source stack.
* Alert thresholds for error rate and latency (for example error rate above 2% or p95 above 800 ms over 5 minutes).
* Alert channel and recipients: email, chat or on-call tool, and who is on duty during the pilot.
* Log retention period, given that the Municipality is the data controller and logs may contain personal data.
* Whether the mobile and web apps must also send client-side errors (out of scope for this ticket unless decided).

## Acceptance criteria
* All back-end services write structured logs in a single agreed format, with a request ID on every entry.
* No personal data in clear text appears in the logs (checked on a sample).
* Metrics for request count, error rate and latency are visible on a dashboard in Staging.
* An alert is triggered and received on the agreed channel when a test error or latency threshold is exceeded.
* Logs, metrics and alerts are stored and processed only in an EU data center.
* Retention period is configured as decided by the PO.

## References
* Requirement RNF-42
* Constraint V-2 (data in EU data centers)

## Context
RF-005 requires that a user can delete the account after exporting data. Personal data must be removed within 30 days and public ads must be anonymized. It depends on RF-003 and RF-040.

## User story
As a user, I want to delete my account, so that my personal data are removed from the platform.

## Scope / Action
* API to request account deletion, after re-authentication of the user.
* Check that the export step was done before accepting the request.
* Deactivate the account immediately and block login.
* Scheduled job that removes personal data within 30 days of the request, including backups according to the agreed policy.
* Anonymize public ads: remove the author's identity and keep the content.
* Handle blocked cases (for example the only referent of a garden).
* Must not break: data of other users, shared records such as shifts and diary entries of gardens.

## Dependencies
* Personal data export story of RF-005.
* RF-003 and RF-040 must be available.

## Points to clarify
* Whether the user can cancel the request within the 30 days (proposed: yes, by logging in).
* How shared records (diary entries, shifts) are handled: anonymize or delete.
* Treatment of backups and logs.
* Behaviour for users who are the only referent of a garden.
* Wording of the confirmation email, if any.

## Acceptance criteria
* After the request the user cannot use the account for new actions.
* Personal data are removed within 30 days of the request.
* Public ads of the user remain visible without the user's name or contact data.
* A request without a completed export is rejected.
* Data of other users are not changed.
* All processing stays in the EU.

## References
* Requirement RF-005
* Requirements RF-003 and RF-040

## Context
Requirement RF-010 needs a back-end that lets Web and Mobile search gardens by position, distance and lot availability, and return data to show them on a map.

## User story
As a user, I want to search gardens by position, distance and lot availability, so that I can find a garden near me with free lots.

## Scope / Action
* Search endpoint with filters: position (coordinates or address), maximum distance, lot availability.
* Response with the data needed for list and map: garden id, name, coordinates, distance, number of free lots.
* Geocoding of addresses through the map provider, with data kept in EU data centres (constraint V-2).
* Availability computed from the lot status defined in RF-012.
* Endpoint usable by guests without login.
* Pagination and sorting by distance.

## Dependencies
* Garden data model and garden detail API of RF-011.
* Lot data and status of RF-012.
* External: map provider.

## Points to clarify
* Map provider to use (must respect EU data location, V-2). Decision for PO.
* Default search radius and maximum number of results.
* Whether "availability" means at least one free lot or a minimum number of lots.

## Acceptance criteria
* A search with position and distance returns only gardens within that distance, sorted by distance.
* The availability filter returns only gardens with at least one lot in status free.
* A guest can call the endpoint without authentication.
* The response contains the fields needed to draw markers on a map.
* Empty results return an empty list, not an error.

## References
* Requirement RF-010. Related requirements: RF-011, RF-012.
